sleeve_length.instruction: Return one value for the garment sleeve itself, not an undershirt, gloves, or sleeves rolled up for styling. Consider the original sleeve endpoint. If the design has genuinely incompatible sleeve lengths and no single label describes it, outside_schema is permitted.

values.Sleeveless: No sleeve extends over the upper arm; shoulder straps are not sleeves.
values.Short Sleeve: A sleeve covering part of the upper arm and ending above the elbow, including cap sleeves.
values.Three-Quarter Sleeve: A sleeve ending below the elbow and before the wrist. In this project, an explicit cropped sleeve description also maps here.
values.Long Sleeve: A full-length sleeve reaching the wrist or beyond.

neckline.instruction: Return one value for the front neckline of the target garment. A low back does not make the front a V-Neck. Do not classify a separate garment worn underneath.

values.Crewneck: A relatively close, rounded neckline at the base of the neck.
values.Scoop Neck: A visibly lower and wider rounded or U-shaped neckline.
values.V-Neck: A front neckline with sides converging to a V-shaped point.
values.High Neck: A neckline rising up the neck: turtleneck, mock neck, funnel neck or similar; an ordinary crewneck is not High Neck.
values.Other: A neckline outside the offered labels, such as boat, square, sweetheart, cowl, straight-across or asymmetric. A collar belongs here when Collared is not an offered label.

strap_style.instruction: Return one value for the upper-body and shoulder construction. Distinctive construction takes precedence over an ordinary configuration; use Other for an unlisted combination that cannot be represented faithfully by one label. The mere presence of sleeves does not establish a standard shoulder construction.

values.Standard: An ordinary sleeveless upper construction with two shoulder straps or two conventional shoulder sections, without the special constructions listed below.
values.Standard Sleeved: A conventional sleeved upper construction with covered shoulders, without off-shoulder, one-shoulder, halter or other special construction.
values.Racerback: Shoulder straps or back panels converge into a central athletic Y/T-shaped back; ordinary crossed straps are not necessarily racerback.
values.Halter: The upper garment is supported around or behind the neck, rather than by two ordinary shoulder straps.
values.One-Shoulder: An asymmetric upper construction supported on or covering one shoulder.
values.Strapless: A strap-free upper construction with neither shoulder nor neck support. Do not infer absence of sleeves solely from this label.
values.Off-Shoulder: An upper edge sitting below the shoulders and exposing both shoulder tops; do not confuse with a low neckline that retains ordinary shoulder support.
values.Other: Another upper construction, e.g. a distinct crossed-back arrangement or a combination not represented by one offered label.

strap_width.instruction: Return one value for the actual shoulder-support fabric, not the neckline binding. Look at front and back views. A sleeveless garment with broad shoulder sections counts as having broad straps for this taxonomy.

values.Spaghetti: Very thin cord-like or narrow ribbon straps.
values.Wide: Clearly broad straps or broad shoulder sections; not merely thicker than a spaghetti strap.
values.Other: Intermediate-width straps, different widths on the two sides, or another width configuration outside the offered labels.
values.Not Applicable: Use only for a strapless upper construction or, where supported by this category, a conventional sleeved upper construction. Do not use it merely because straps are difficult to see.
